searchText: Post-Gloas Prysm and Teku gossip DoS thread We were able to DoS a teku node with fewer empty txs about 1 million of them. Slightly different attack vector this time: Builder bid accepted, beacon root known but signed envelope is not revealed. Instead, the builder sends lots of structurally valid signed envelopes (valid BLS G2 point + subgroup) but hundreds of such 1M tx envelopes. These are decoded and deserialized: the hash tree root of such high cardinality tx envelopes keeps the signed envelope queue drain rate slower than memory accumulation. excerpts.author: bshastry
excerpts.content: We were able to DoS a teku node with fewer empty txs about 1 million of them. Slightly different attack vector this time: Builder bid accepted, beacon root known but signed envelope is not revealed. Instead, the builder sends lots of structurally valid signed envelopes (valid BLS G2 point + subgroup) but hundreds of such 1M tx envelopes. These are decoded and deserialized: the hash tree root of such high cardinality tx envelopes keeps the signed envelope queue drain rate slower than memory accumulation.
